question.text: A company with assets of INR 200 crore and liabilities of INR 80 crore has book value of:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that asset-based valuation uses the market value of assets less liabilities, and that book value or NAV uses assets and liabilities at historical carrying cost, with book value per share based on equity shareholders' funds. Applying assets minus liabilities: 200 - 80 = INR 120 crore. The Trap: INR 80 crore is the liabilities figure alone. INR 200 crore is the gross asset value before deducting liabilities. INR 280 crore incorrectly adds rather than subtracts liabilities. Note: The earlier explanation was generic placeholder text. It has been replaced with the source-backed assets-minus-liabilities / book-value calculation drawn from the workbook's asset-based valuation discussion.
